speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful? Also, have you had any recent fevers, sore throats, or exposures to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless, nonpruritic nature of the papules and the recent exposure to chickenpox, I suspect an unrelated viral exanthem. Have the lesions spread to other areas of the body, and have you noticed any changes in their appearance, such as central clearing or umbilication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
